sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner; Sri Ambrish Shukla, learned Additional Chief Standing
Counsel for the State-respondent and Sri Kaushalendra Nath Singh, learned counsel for the
respondent
Nos. 3 & 4 - Noida.

2. The present writ petition is preferred praying inter alia with the following principal relief:
"I) A writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent nos.
2 and 3 to take appropriate action for correction of the name of the petitioners in the
revenue record, which was illegally recorded in the name of Noida in the revenue
record in between 1.7.2014 to 30.6.2020 in the Khatauni for Fasli Year 1422 to 1427,
over the land i.e. Khasra No. 11-M, Khata No. 118, area 100 square foot or 83.61
square meter, which is situated at Garhi Chaukhandi, Tehsil Dadri, District Gautam
Buddha Nagar."
3.  In the instant matter, vide order dated 31.10.2025, we have asked the learned counsel for the NOIDA to get instructions regarding the case.
Today, Sri Kaushalendra Nath Singh, learned counsel for the NOIDA, has placed detailed instructions, which is taken on record.
He submits that the dispute relates to Khasra No. 11 (total area 2.9660 hectare).
He submits that for planned development, the State Government initiated acquisition proceedings for the land situated at Garhi Chaukhandi, Tehsil Dadri, District Gautam Buddha Nagar.
A notification under Section 4(1), read with Section 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act, 1894"), was issued on 11.9.2006.

Thereafter, final declaration under Section 6, read with Section 17(1) of the Act,
1894, was issued on 27.10.2006 and the actual physical possession was also taken by the competent authority on 2.12.2006.
He further submits that out of total 2.9660 hectare land, the State Government had acquired 2.9500 hectare and rest 0.0160 hectare land remained with the irrigation department.
Later on the relevant entry also took place in the revenue record.
Admittedly, the petitioner had purchased the land in question on 14.5.2007.

He argues that once the Collector has made an award under Section 11 of the Act, 1894, the Government may take possession of the land,
which then vests absolutely in the Government, free from all encumbrances.

He submits that it is settled law that after the notification under Section 4(1) is published in the Gazette, any encumbrance created by the owner does not bind the Government, and the purchaser does not acquire any title to the property.
In this case, the notification under Section 4(1) was published on 11.9.2006, and the alleged purchase took place on 14.5.2007.

Consequently,
the land vested in the State under Section 17(2), free from all encumbrances.

He has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in V. Chandrasekaran & Ors. vs. The Administrative Officer & Ors., (2012) 12 SCC 133, where the Court opined that after the issuance of a notification under Section 4 of the Act, 1894, a purchaser has no right to challenge the acquisition but is entitled to compensation as he steps into the shoes of the original landowner.

entities.text: V. Chandrasekaran & Ors. vs. The Administrative Officer & Ors., (2012) 12 SCC 133
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the judgment is reproduced below:

"18. In view of the above, the law on the issue can be summarized to the effect that a person who purchases land subsequent to the issuance of a Section 4 notification with respect to it, is not competent to challenge the validity of the acquisition proceedings on any ground whatsoever, for the reason that the sale deed executed in his favour does not confer upon him, any title and at the most he can claim compensation on the basis of his vendor's title."

4. The learned counsel for the NOIDA further submits that a similar view was taken by the Apex Court in U.P. Jal Nigam v. M/s. Kalra Properties Pvt. Ltd., (1996) 3 SCC 124, where the Hon'ble Apex Court held that a sale made after the publication of the notification under Section 4(1) of the Act, 1894, is void against the State.

entities.text: U.P. Jal Nigam v. M/s. Kalra Properties Pvt. Ltd., (1996) 3 SCC 124
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case, M/s. Kalra Properties had no right, title, or interest in the land and could not challenge the validity of the notification or the acquisition.

It was held that any encumbrance created after the notification under Section 4(1) does not bind the Government,
and the purchaser is merely entitled to claim compensation, stepping into the shoes of the original owner.
He has also placed reliance on the judgment dated 05.09.2022, passed in Writ-C No. 30608 of 2018 (M/s Tanuj Dwivedi and Ajay Kumar Singh, Advocates vs. State of U.P. and others).

entities.text: Ajay Kumar Singh, Advocates vs. State of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Lastly,
he submits that if the original owner has not lifted the compensation, the petitioner, if entitled, may approach the Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) for the disbursement of compensation,
provided there are no legal impediments.
5. In the instant matter, we have considered the claim set up by the petitioner and the objections raised by the learned counsel for the NOIDA.

Firstly, it is an admitted fact that the encumbrance was created after the issuance of the notification under Section 4, read with Section 17(4) of the Act,
1894.
Therefore, we are of the considered opinion that the sale is void against the State, and the petitioner has acquired no right, title, or interest in the land.
Secondly, it is settled law that the petitioner cannot challenge the validity of the notification or the legality of the possession taken.

However, we find that the petitioner/subsequent purchaser, as a person interested in the compensation stepping into the shoes of the erstwhile owner, is entitled to claim the compensation it if it has not been lifted by the erstwhile owner.
6. Accordingly, we dispose of the writ petition with the observation that in case the petitioner is entitled to compensation, definitely she may press the relief before the competent forum.
